title: Boss: pick the technique
summary: Four problems, four techniques: one pass, prefix sums with a dictionary, a sliding window, and a 2D table.

steps.title: Which tool?
body: Each challenge has an obvious `O(n²)` (or worse) answer and a faster one. Before coding, ask:
| "best so far" while scanning once | a running min or max |
| sums of ranges, counted many times | prefix sums plus a `Dictionary` |
| the shortest/longest contiguous run with a property | a sliding window |
| answers built from answers to smaller inputs | DP with a table |
Every test set is big enough that only the fast approach finishes.

steps.title: Best time to buy and sell
prompt: `prices[i]` is a share price on day `i`. Buy once and sell once on a **later** day. Write `int MaxProfit(int[] prices)`: the largest profit, or 0 if no trade makes money.
One pass: remember the cheapest price so far; each day, selling today would earn `price - cheapest`.
template: Dojo.Eq("selling must come after buying", 2, MaxProfit(new[] { 9, 1, 3, 0, 2 }));
hints: Update `cheapest` first, then `best = Math.Max(best, p - cheapest)`.

steps.title: Subarrays that sum to k
prompt: Write `long SubarraysWithSum(int[] a, int k)`: how many contiguous subarrays add up to exactly `k`. Values can be negative, so a sliding window does not work.

Prefix sums: a subarray ending here sums to `k` exactly when an **earlier** prefix sum equals `running - k`. Keep a `Dictionary<long, int>` counting the prefix sums seen so far, starting with `{ 0: 1 }` for the empty prefix. The tests use 200,000 values.
hints: Start the dictionary with `{ [0] = 1 }`: the empty prefix lets a subarray starting at index 0 be counted.
For each value: add it to `running`, add `seen[running - k]` (if any) to the count, then record `running`.

steps.title: Shortest run reaching a target
prompt: All values are **positive**. Write `int ShortestRun(int[] a, int target)`: the length of the shortest contiguous run whose sum is **at least** `target`, or 0 if none.
Sliding window: grow on the right; while the window's sum is at least `target`, record its length and shrink from the left. The tests use 300,000 values.
template: Dojo.Eq("a single item is enough", 1, ShortestRun(new[] { 1, 4, 4 }, 4));
hints: Add `a[right]` to `sum`. Then, as long as `sum >= target`, update `best` and remove `a[left]` while moving `left` right.

steps.title: Longest common subsequence
prompt: A **subsequence** keeps characters in order but may skip some: `ace` is a subsequence of `abcde`. Write `int Lcs(string a, string b)`: the length of the longest subsequence common to both. `diff` tools are built on this.
DP with a 2D table: `dp[i, j]` is the LCS of the first `i` characters of `a` and the first `j` of `b`.
- otherwise: `dp[i, j] = Math.Max(dp[i - 1, j], dp[i, j - 1])`
Row 0 and column 0 are 0. The tests compare two 2,000-character strings: 4 million cells.
solution: dp[i, j] = a[i - 1] == b[j - 1] ? dp[i - 1, j - 1] + 1 : Math.Max(dp[i - 1, j], dp[i, j - 1]);
hints: Two nested loops, `i` from 1 to `a.Length` and `j` from 1 to `b.Length`.
Matching characters extend the diagonal; otherwise take the better of dropping a character from either string.
